desc:
An undirected tree has n nodes numbered 0..n-1 and n - 1 edges [a, b]. A longest path is a path between two nodes with the maximum possible number of edges (the diameter). A tree may have many different longest paths.

Return how many nodes lie on at least one longest path.

n = 7, edges = [[0,1],[1,2],[2,3],[3,4],[2,5],[1,6]]

the diameter is 4 and the longest paths are 0-1-2-3-4 and 6-1-2-3-4
nodes on them: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6   -> 6   (node 5 is on none)
constraints: edges.length = n - 1 and the edges form a tree
A single node is a path of length 0 and lies on it, so n = 1 gives 1
hints: First find the diameter D. Then the question is which nodes can be an inner point or end of a path of exactly D edges.
For a node v, look at the longest chains that start at v and leave it through different neighbours. A path of length D passes through v exactly when the two longest such chains add up to D.

Compute down[v] (height of v's subtree) and up[v] (longest chain starting at v and going first to its parent) with a downward pass and an upward pass; for each node take the top two branch lengths (chains through different neighbours, plus 0), and count the nodes where they sum to the maximum over all nodes.
editorial: For any node v, every branch from v goes out through one neighbour. Let the branch lengths be the longest chain starting at v and leaving through each neighbour. The best path passing through v has length equal to the sum of the two longest branch lengths (a missing branch counts as 0, which makes v an end of the path). The diameter D is the maximum of this value over all v, and v lies on a longest path exactly when its value equals D.

Compute the branches with rerooting. Root the tree at 0. down[v] is the longest chain going down from v (0 for a leaf). For a child c of p, the branch of p through c has length down[c] + 1. The branch of v going up is up[v] = 1 + max(up[p], best branch of p through a child other than v), where up of the root is treated as 0. To get 'best other child' in O(1), keep the two largest child branches of each node.

Then for each node collect its branch values (child branches and, for non-roots, the up branch), take the two largest (pad with 0), and sum them. Take the maximum as D and count nodes that reach it. Everything is O(n) with two passes over a BFS order.
